reason: The giant can redirect the distant icy bodies, directly addressing the first goal.
expectation: I expect the giant's gravity to send some icy bodies inward, though their eventual paths are uncertain.

alternatives.reason: The fragments crossing the rings may address the other goal, but I chose to follow the ice first.

effect: The giant sent icy bodies inward along several possible paths, so I can now follow one of them.
reaction: The different routes make me curious about how the ice changes near the star.
reason: Taking the icy bodies into warm space follows their inward journey and may show what happens to their ice.
expectation: I expect some ice to turn into gas as the bodies warm, though some solid material may remain.

alternatives.reason: Crossing the rocky worlds' orbits is another interesting route, but I want to see the warming first.

effect: The warming ice releases gas and embedded dust, while a cold remnant can survive. I can follow another inward path.
reaction: The immense thin cloud trailing a small remnant is a striking image.
reason: Following the icy bodies across the rocky worlds' orbits may show where else the giant sends them.
expectation: Some icy bodies may encounter the rocky worlds, though they could also pass without striking them.

alternatives.reason: The fragments crossing the giant's rings could also address the other goal, but I want to finish following the ice first.

effect: The icy bodies struck rocky worlds and completed the ice goal; I can now follow the remaining fragments.
reaction: The uncertainty about how much water survives the impacts is interesting.
reason: The fragments can cross the giant's rings, offering one path for matter that missed the worlds.
expectation: I expect the fragments to collide with or disturb ring material, though their fate is uncertain.

alternatives.reason: The fragments could also be followed through warm space, but I want to see their encounter with the rings first.

effect: The rocky fragment's impact sprays ring ice above the ring plane; the remaining offered action follows fragments through warm space.
reaction: The spray makes the apparently smooth rings feel dynamic.
reason: This is the only available combination and follows another fate for the leftover fragments.
expectation: I expect the fragments to change or disperse in warm space, though their precise fate is uncertain.

effect: The leftover stones collide and produce fine dust; the remaining combination can bring it together with material released from the ice.
reaction: The progression from larger fragments to dust makes sense, though it is fairly predictable.
reason: This is the only offered combination and follows the two sources of material in warm space.
expectation: I expect the rocky dust to mingle with the gas and dust released from warming ice, though I am unsure what that produces.

effect: The two dust sources mingle and scatter starlight, completing the remaining goal.
reaction: The faint glow is a satisfying way to bring the two paths together.

mostWorthwhile.text: Bringing dust from collisions and warming ice together was worthwhile because it connected two distinct paths into one visible result.

leastWorthwhile.text: Grinding leftover stones into dust felt fairly predictable, especially as it was the only offered combination.

surprise.text: A small icy remnant can trail an immense, thin cloud of released gas and grains.

arbitrary.text: No action felt especially arbitrary; the final mixing followed naturally from the two sources, although it was the only offered combination.

continue.text: Yes. I would be curious to follow how the dispersed material changes later; the converging dust paths made a satisfying ending.
